name: Queer Wellness 🛁🫧 Marts 2026
description:
DANSK
Velkommen til Queer Wellness forår 2026 💙 Vi byder på badekar, saunagus, afslapning og backgammon i Sjællandsgade Badet for alle queer voksne hen over vinteren og lidt til.

Lejlighedsvist har vi cute pop-ups: Førhen har vi haft croquis, massage, Queer Cut, (Un)told og cute DJs på programmet. Vi annoncerer i den pågældende begivenhed, hvis der sker noget særligt 🛁 💿

PRAKTISK
🫧 Køkultur og først-til-mølle: Der er cirka plads til 50 personer. Dørene lukker, når der er fyldt.  
🫧 Donationsbaseret entré med sliding scale. Donér, hvad du kan, og hvad du tænker giver mening; alle beløb er helt okay.  
🫧 Sjællandsgade Badet er ikke niveaufrit.  
🫧 Husk håndklæde. Du bestemmer selv, hvor på- eller afklædt du vil være.  

HUSREGLER  
🫧 Queer Wellness er et rum med nøgenhed. Husk: Pronominer og køn kan ikke aflæses fra en krop. Antag ikke andres pronominer eller køn.  
🫧 Vi lader mobilen blive i tasken. Ingen fotos eller videoer er tilladt.  
🫧 Vi siger nej til racisme, transfobi, bifobi, femmefobi, homofobi, sexisme, queerfobi osv.  
🫧 Queer Wellness er et alkohol- og rusmiddelfrit rum.  

Lad os sammen skabe et tryggere rum ved at overholde husreglerne. Hvis du oplever, at husreglerne brydes, eller du på nogen måde føler dig utilpas, så tøv ikke med at komme til os, der arrangerer aftenen. Vi er typisk at finde i køkkenet i stuen og ved indgangen.

OM FLINT
Queer Wellness er drevet af frivillige fra det queerfeministiske initiativ Flint KBH. Vi er nonprofit og har tilhørsforhold i Kvindehuset på Gothersgade 37.
______________________
ENGLISH
Welcome to Queer Wellness 💙 We offer bathtubs, sauna, relaxation, and backgammon, in Sjællandsgade Badet, for all queer adults during the winter.

Occasionally, we host cute pop-ups: In the past, we’ve had croquis, massage, Queer Cut, (Un)customs, and cute DJs on the programme. We'll announce in the respective event if something special is happening 🛁 💿

PRACTICAL
🫧 Queue culture and first-come, first-served: There is space for approximately 50 people. Doors close when full.  
🫧 Donation-based entrance with a sliding scale. Donate what you can and what you think makes sense. Any amount is fine.  
🫧 Sjællandsgade Badet is not step-free.  
🫧 Remember to bring a towel. You decide how dressed or undressed you want to be.  

HOUSE RULES
🫧 Queer Wellness is a space with nudity. Remember: Pronouns and gender cannot be determined from a body. Do not assume the pronouns or gender of others.  
🫧 We leave our phones in our bags. No photos or videos are allowed.  
🫧 We say no to racism, transphobia, biphobia, femmephobia, homophobia, sexism, queerphobia, etc.  
🫧 Queer Wellness is an alcohol- and drug-free space.  

Let's create a safer space together by following the house rules. If you experience that any of the house rules are being broken or you feel uncomfortable in any way, don't hesitate to come to us, the organisers of the evening. We are typically to be found in the kitchen on the first floor or at the entrance.

ABOUT FLINT
Queer Wellness is run by volunteers from the queer feminist initiative Flint KBH. We are nonprofit and are located in Kvindehuset at Gothersgade 37.

name: DUG (IE)
description:
There’s a natural magnetism to DUG’s folk brew. The duo, made up of Conor (Lorkin) O’Reilly and Jonny Pickett, are gearing up for the release of their debut album, having formed in 2023–but you’d be forgiven for believing that they’ve been writing together for a lifetime.

Their music stems from roots in musical traditions spanning both sides of the pond. In one breath, echoing the great American folk troubadours, and in another, comfortably channelling the elder statesmen of Irish folk.

This is no accident. DUG have a shared musical heritage, with members having been born in America and Scotland before arriving in Ireland. O’Reilly himself spent almost a decade making and releasing music in upstate New York, having picked up sticks from his native Edinburgh, (Irish mother and Scottish father) before moving to Ireland in 2022 to start a new musical chapter.

And you can hear that lived musical experience in singles like ‘Big Sundown’ and ‘Jubilee’ (shortlisted for two Grammy nominations). Resonator guitar and banjo, the building blocks of DUG’s arrangements, lick and spin, with intricate finger-picking patterns whirling to a compelling whole. Their music breathes, vamping in sync.

They’re damn funny too. DUG’s lyrics catch you off guard, eliciting an honest-to-goodness chuckle in a moment of levity. At their very best, as on their forthcoming album, there’s a bona fide warmth littered throughout their unique take on folk storytelling. Tracks like ‘Wheel of Fortune’ have an easy rapport.  It’s catching up with an old friend, all mischief and smiles.

There are allusions to darker moments there too; yearning and melancholy, to lessons learnt the hard way. Taking the heavy with the light, and being able to translate it into a foot-tapping, infectious contemporary folk sound is what DUG do best. They don’t need to posture; their music is naturally playful and honest, inviting you along on their musical journey.

DUG’s love for the musicians that inspired them never steps too far into reverence. They’re an unapologetically modern band. You’ll hear plenty of Irish influence in their music, but you’ll not find any tweed coats or paddy caps here. Instead, the band opts to be themselves-completely natural and organic. It’s part of what gives the group’s work such a strong charisma, and helps establish DUG as having one of the most unique takes on contemporary folk music.

In 2024, the duo signed to Claddagh Records, a label in which they find themselves in fine musical company. A subsidiary of Universal Records, Claddagh Records has spent the last few years becoming a hotbed for some of the most forward-thinking musicians in contemporary Irish folk, home to artists like Niamh Bury, Lemoncello, and ØXN, to name a few.

It should come as no surprise that a group that delights in a touch of devilment and so ardently remains true to themselves has built a thriving community of fans, both at their live shows and through their often hilarious social media.
